scenes.caption: Docket keeps invoice expectations and payment evidence in one review desk.
This is a real Sepolia transfer with an illustrative invoice, not customer work.
The expected recipient and exact amount stay beside the source transaction.
A random salt keeps the invoice fingerprint from revealing private details.
First, read the source receipt and compare the transfer with the expectation.
The call succeeded and the recipient and amount match. Inclusion is still unchecked.
Now Attestcoin builds a proof and Creditcoin checks transaction inclusion.
Inclusion is verified. It is separate from payment matching and invoice ownership.
A public registry write is a separate step. It is still waiting for free testnet gas.
Leave a note describing exactly what the evidence supports.
Reviewed requires a successful receipt, an exact transfer match and real inclusion.
Save the decision with its note so the next review has context.
The public export leaves out invoice text, the salt and reviewer notes.
A separate private bundle is for a chosen reviewer or your own backup.
Earlier network checks stay in the export. A new check does not rewrite them.
The saved record survives a reload. The private data stays in this browser.
Docket makes the evidence clear before a team marks a payment record reviewed.
